review_notes: I read the whole file and the helper lemmas it uses in CTCasesE6Arith.lean (not_dvd_of_pow_ne_one, pow_ne_one_of_orderOf, ordProj_eq_of_int_factor). The three ordProj_twisted_* theorems repeat the same non-divisibility reasoning and the same large LHS. The helper lemmas at the top (cast_pow_sub_one, not_dvd_pow_sub_one, not_dvd_pow_add_one, not_dvd_pow, ordProj_eq_of_int_cofactor) are already factored well. I did not compile anything, so the proposed lemma is untested. The saving is moderate because the cofactors R differ per case: the eight case has no q^8-1 and no q^2-1 in R, the twelve case factors q^4-1 and q^2+q+1 differently, and the eighteen case uses q^3+1. A core lemma therefore only covers the factors that all three cases share. I did not check whether the same duplication also occurs inside CTCasesE6Arith.lean beyond the grep hits.

findings.problem: All three theorems rerun the same argument. First they derive hpz from hp. Then they derive ¬p ∣ q^36, ¬p ∣ q^6-1 and ¬p ∣ q^5+1 from the order hypothesis, each by its own `show ¬ m ∣ _ by norm_num` side goal. Then they combine these (with others) by a hand-nested chain of hpz.not_dvd_mul. Finally they close with the same `refine ordProj_eq_of_int_cofactor ... simp only [Nat.cast_mul, cast_pow_sub_one ...]; ring` tail. The three-factor core q^36*(q^6-1)*(q^5+1) is the same in all three and is rebuilt each time at the cost of a differently shaped, error-prone not_dvd_mul nesting (lines 60-61, 88-89, 111-112). The long LHS `q ^ 36 * (q ^ 12 - 1) * ...` is also copied verbatim into all three statements.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a shared lemma before the three theorems:

theorem not_dvd_twisted_core {p q m : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hpq : ¬ p ∣ q)
    (hord : orderOf (q : ZMod p) = m) (h6 : ¬ m ∣ 6) (h5 : ¬ m ∣ 2 * 5) :
    ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ (q : ℤ) ^ 36 * ((q : ℤ) ^ 6 - 1) * ((q : ℤ) ^ 5 + 1)

Proof sketch: `have hpz := Nat.prime_iff_prime_int.mp hp; exact hpz.not_dvd_mul (hpz.not_dvd_mul (not_dvd_pow hp hpq 36) (not_dvd_pow_sub_one hord h6)) (not_dvd_pow_add_one hord h5)`.

Also introduce a local `abbrev`/`def twistedN (q : ℕ) : ℕ := q ^ 36 * (q ^ 12 - 1) * (q ^ 9 + 1) * (q ^ 8 - 1) * (q ^ 6 - 1) * (q ^ 5 + 1) * (q ^ 2 - 1)` for the shared left-hand side.

Each theorem then supplies only its own extra factors. For example, in the eight case take R := core * (((q:ℤ)^12-1) * ((q:ℤ)^9+1) * ((q:ℤ)^4-1)) and the proof `hpz.not_dvd_mul (not_dvd_twisted_core hp hpq hord (by norm_num) (by norm_num)) (hpz.not_dvd_mul (hpz.not_dvd_mul h12 h9) h4)`. In the twelve and eighteen cases the same core replaces h36/h6/h5 and the remaining extra-factor hypotheses (h4, h3, h9, h8, h2 for twelve; h12, h3, h8, h2 for eighteen) are combined separately. The `ring` closing step absorbs the reassociation, so the hfac goals are unchanged.
findings.benefit: The common non-divisibility argument is stated and proved once, and the three proofs shrink to only their case-specific factors and casts. The deeply nested `hpz.not_dvd_mul` chains are the part most likely to break when a factor is changed. Making the shared left-hand side a single named definition means the three statements cannot drift apart.

evidence.excerpt: have h6 := not_dvd_pow_sub_one hord (show ¬ 12 ∣ 6 by norm_num)
have h5 := not_dvd_pow_add_one hord (show ¬ 18 ∣ 2 * 5 by norm_num)
